[head=2][color=#bf4d00]New Crescent Worker's League[/color][/head]
The NCWL was born from a workers' uprising in the Crescent Sector, where loose gangs of laborers and unions collectivized into a nation. They run on socialist ideals and the promise of freedom for all, which makes rivals dismiss them as naive. Underestimating them is a mistake, because the League is vast, industrious, and utterly committed.
Culturally the Union rejects lords and titles. Rank exists for the sake of the fight rather than for privilege, and everyone is a [bold]comrade[/bold] in the struggle.
[head=3][color=#bf4d00]Command[/color][/head]
- [bold]Flagman.[/bold] The faction leader and the voice of the League on the field. - [bold]Unionkapitan.[/bold] The fleet commander who directs the League's ships. - [bold]Kommissar.[/bold] A political and military officer who keeps units in line and morale high. - [bold]Kommissar Cadet.[/bold] A Kommissar in training, learning to lead.
[head=3][color=#bf4d00]Soldiers[/color][/head]
- [bold]Partisan.[/bold] The backbone infantry of the League and the everyday frontline fighter. - [bold]Starshina.[/bold] An MVD grunt who handles internal security. - [bold]Homeguard Militiaman.[/bold] Militia raised for defense and wartime call-ups. - [bold]Union Worker.[/bold] The newcomer's role, a laborer taking up arms.
[head=3][color=#bf4d00]Industry and Support[/color][/head]
- [bold]Sindikat Overseer[/bold] and [bold]Sindikat Artificer.[/bold] They run the League's factories and produce its war material. - [bold]Logistics Coordinator[/bold] and [bold]Logistics Crew.[/bold] They keep supplies and cargo moving. - [bold]Alyans Director[/bold] and [bold]Alyans Sanitar.[/bold] They form the League's medical corps.
[head=3][color=#bf4d00]How to address them[/color][/head]
Everyone is a [color=#bf4d00][bold]Comrade[/bold][/color], as in "Comrade Kapitan" or "well fought, comrade." Civilians and workers may also be called [color=#bf4d00][bold]Citizen[/bold][/color]. Officers are addressed by their post, such as Kommissar, Unionkapitan, or Flagman, and never by any lordly title.
[color=#d9776c]Never[/color] use "Sir," "My Lord," or any noble honorific with a Union member. To them that is Imperial language, and using it sincerely marks you as an enemy or a bootlicker. See the [color=#e8b04b]Forms of Address[/color] page for more.
